note: The class reached NSCLC after nivolumab and pembrolizumab (non-members) had answered the question; the four members ran on MC38 mice and monkey receptor-occupancy data, and three (camrelizumab, toripalimab, dostarlimab) met first-line NSCLC endpoints, while toripalimab's monkeys missed the immune-related harms the knockout mouse and dostarlimab's monkeys had foretold and camrelizumab's haemangiomas were explained only by a post-hoc off-target screen.
label: NSCLC (anti-PD-1)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Toripalimab (JS-001) was first dosed in patients in March 2016 (Wei 2020), so the monkey work predates this 2017 paper; 2017 is its first public date.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
engagement.note: JS-001 at 1 and 10 mg/kg cut PD-1+ T-cell staining in vaccinated monkeys, read as receptor occupancy; no patient occupancy had been reported.
engagement.short: Monkey RO readout, no patient data yet
engagement.quote: intramuscular injection of JS-001 (1 and 10 mg/kg) resulted in dramatic decreases in PD-1+/CD4+ and PD-1+/CD8+ expression in a dose-dependent manner, which was supported by PD-1 receptor occupancy (RO) results.

engagement.magnitude_basis: fraction of PD-1 occupied on T cells: saturating in monkeys at 1-10 mg/kg vs >80% in patients from 0.3 mg/kg
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT02915432 registry results posting not looked up. Patients were mixed refractory solid tumours; engagement does not require the context disease.
engagement.judgement: Pairing is mine (comparison_stated false): Fu 2017 monkey RO against Wei 2020 patient RO. Dostarlimab (Kumar 2021, 10.1007/s00280-021-04358-3; FDA review 2021) also showed maximal RO at every dose, but no public dostarlimab monkey RO datum exists to pair it with, so it is noted, not scored. Camrelizumab Phase 1 (Mo 2018) measured RO but gives no number in the abstract.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
engagement.note: Toripalimab Phase 1: complete (>80%) PD-1 occupancy on activated T cells from the first dose at every level including 0.3 mg/kg, as monkeys predicted.
engagement.short: Patient PD-1 occupancy >80% as in monkeys
engagement.quote: Most patients, including those from the 0.3 mg/kg group, maintained complete PD-1 receptor occupancy (> 80%) on activated T cells since receiving the first dose of toripalimab.

engagement.model: NSG mice reconstituted with human PBMCs, with T-cell expansion and effector-memory proportion as the PD readout (toripalimab Studies 34885_IVHU and TR003)
engagement.note: Toripalimab 10 mg/kg on Days 0/1 and 6 raised splenic CD3+, CD4+ and CD8+ human T-cell frequency and the effector-memory proportion by two weeks.
engagement.short: huPBMC mice: T-cell expansion, no patient test
engagement.quote: In vivo, in mice engrafted with human PBMCs, toripalimab promoted T cell expansion. Specifically, toripalimab increased the proportion of effector memory T cells.
engagement.confidence_note: Review pp.43 and 48-49 read in full. Two studies: 34885_IVHU (TAB001 clones 38 and 41, nivolumab as positive control; circulating cells unchanged on Day 6, spleen raised on Day 13) and TR003 (frozen PBMCs, two weeks). Both undated and pre-2016; 2023 is the first public date.
engagement.judgement: Kept apart from the CTL-engrafted MC38 track: whole PBMCs, no tumour, and a PD readout (T-cell expansion) rather than tumour growth. The monkey track reads receptor occupancy (direct); this one reads a downstream cellular response, so it is not the same system either.

engagement.model: NSG mice reconstituted with human PBMCs, with T-cell expansion and effector-memory proportion as the PD readout (toripalimab Studies 34885_IVHU and TR003)
engagement.note: Oesophageal patients on camrelizumab plus radiotherapy: CD8 proliferation rose as the mice predicted, but effector-memory share did not. Combination ruling: a member with another active treatment is scored as given.
engagement.short: Patient CD8 proliferation rose, subsets unchanged
engagement.quote: this therapy decreased PD-1 expression by the 4 subsets and TIGIT expression by effector memory T cells, as well as significantly enhanced the proliferative activity of CD8 T cells, whereas concurrent chemoradiotherapy produced different effects.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 36822161, J Leukoc Biol 113(1):11-17, dated 2023-01-10 on PubMed). Confounded: camrelizumab was given with radiotherapy and the comparator was chemoradiotherapy, not radiotherapy alone; 19 vs 15 patients, oesophageal squamous carcinoma. The sentence before the quote states the four CD8 subset proportions did not change.
engagement.magnitude_basis: human T-cell expansion and effector-memory shift in huPBMC-NSG mice vs Ki67 proliferative activity of peripheral CD8 T cells in patients (subset proportions unchanged)
engagement.judgement: Pairing is mine: the model was dosed with toripalimab, the patients with camrelizumab, a sibling member (product_in_model false). Same in direction, partial because the effector-memory shift the mice showed did not appear. A cleaner patient datum (member-drug monotherapy, Ki67+ CD8 burst) was not found; the PubMed sweep's other hits were combinations with 4-1BB, IL-1beta or CD3 engagers. Engagement does not require the context disease. Rule question settled under the 2026-11-09 combination ruling: a member drug given with another active treatment is scored on what the trial measured, so the radiotherapy co-treatment does not set the entry aside; same with source_calls_it partial stands. No camrelizumab opener: the mice were never dosed with camrelizumab.
engagement.reason: CD8 proliferation rose in dosed patients

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
dose.note: Monkey doses of 1-10 mg/kg produced receptor occupancy; no human exposure or regimen target had yet been tested in patients.
dose.quote: In the PK study, 18 cynomolgus monkeys treated with single, ascending doses of 1, 10, and 75 mg/kg, and another 6 cynomolgus monkeys received 10 mg/kg successive administration.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT03856411 has no posted results. The occupancy-saturating regimen is from Wei 2020 (>80% RO from 0.3 mg/kg), the trial dose 240 mg q3w from this abstract. Earliest public date: Coherus/Junshi press release 2021-08-18 (interim PFS HR 0.58, WCLC 2021 oral on 2021-09-13), https://investors.coherus.com/news-releases/news-release-details/coherus-and-junshi-biosciences-announce-positive-interim-results.
dose.judgement: Scored by the efficacy-tied rule (reached, worked). The occupancy target (saturation) was reached in patients at 0.3 mg/kg and the trial gave 240 mg every 3 weeks, so it was reached and sufficient; no tolerability margin was public before the 2023 FDA review, so margin_stated is null here and true on the next entry.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
dose.note: CHOICE-01: toripalimab 240 mg q3w with chemotherapy, a regimen holding PD-1 saturated, met PFS (HR 0.49). Year 2021: Junshi/Coherus announced the met endpoint on 2021-08-18.
dose.short: Saturating 240 mg q3w reached; PFS met
dose.quote: At the final PFS analysis, PFS was significantly longer in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (median PFS, 8.4 v 5.6 months, hazard ratio = 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.61; two-sided P < .0001).

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL exposure (100 mg/kg weekly, 26 weeks) vs patient AUC at 240 mg q3w: 13-23-fold margin
dose.population: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma and pooled solid tumours on 240 mg q3w (toripalimab programme exposure)
dose.confidence_note: Review read in passages (nonclinical sections 5 and clinical pharmacology); the patient AUC quoted is from the NPC programme, the same regimen used in CHOICE-01.
dose.judgement: Strengthens, not a new status. Decision 16: the monkey stated a tolerated exposure (NOAEL 100 mg/kg, receptor saturated at 30-100 mg/kg) 13-23 times the patient AUC, and patients were dosed to saturation without the monkey's (absent) toxicity, so margin_stated true. FDA also states the patient concentrations sat within the target predicted to keep tumour PD-1 fully occupied (in vitro saturation at 3 ug/mL; trough target 20 ug/mL).
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
dose.note: FDA: monkey exposure at the 26-week NOAEL was 13-23x the patient AUC at 240 mg q3w; patient troughs sat within the full-occupancy target.
dose.quote: Exposure achieved in the monkeys at the 100 mg/kg dose level on Day 92 was 13 to 23-fold higher than the AUC in patients receiving either 240 mg flat dose once every 3 weeks
dose.reason: Saturating dose reached, enough, margin held

dose.model: Population-PK simulation of exposure under the regimen taken into the trial (dostarlimab 500 mg Q3W then 1000 mg Q6W; toripalimab 240 mg Q3W flat dose vs 3 mg/kg Q2W)
dose.note: Dostarlimab's 1000 mg Q6W maintenance was chosen by popPK simulation; PERLA in NSCLC dosed 500 mg Q3W only, so the simulated regimen was never given to NSCLC patients.
dose.quote: Based on model simulations of exposure parameters following either 500 mg Q3W or 1,000 mg Q6W dosing, both Cmin and Cavg were similar across the two treatments.
dose.confidence_note: Review clinical pharmacology section read in passages. The model was built on GARNET (endometrial and other solid tumours); FDA agreed the exposures were similar but called the exposure-response analyses limited and inconclusive. Toripalimab's own popPK (240 mg Q3W vs 3 mg/kg Q2W) became public in the 2023 review and is folded into this track.
dose.judgement: One track for both members' popPK models, by analogy with the draft's single monkey track; each is a sponsor model fit to patient PK and used to pick the regimen carried into the Phase 3. The brief's in-silico dose-model category; prediction_level class.

dose.model: Population-PK simulation of exposure under the regimen taken into the trial (dostarlimab 500 mg Q3W then 1000 mg Q6W; toripalimab 240 mg Q3W flat dose vs 3 mg/kg Q2W)
dose.note: Retrodiction ruling: toripalimab's popPK simulation was first public in 2023, after its own 240 mg Q3W patient PK and CHOICE-01; it reproduced the observed exposure, so retro, not same.
dose.short: Simulated flat regimen reached; PFS met
dose.quote: At the final PFS analysis, PFS was significantly longer in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (median PFS, 8.4 v 5.6 months, hazard ratio = 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.61; two-sided P < .0001).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of CHOICE-01; year 2023 because toripalimab's popPK simulation (95% exposure coverage 88-96% of 3 mg/kg Q2W) was public only in the October 2023 FDA review. PERLA dosed dostarlimab 500 mg Q3W, not the simulated 1000 mg Q6W.
dose.magnitude_basis: observed steady-state Cmax/Cmin at 240 mg Q3W (85/19 ug/mL) vs the 3 mg/kg Q2W reference (77/25 ug/mL) the simulation matched to; simulated 95% exposure coverage 88-96%
dose.judgement: Under the 2026-11-09 retrodiction ruling for dose (only the same drug's own earlier patient result counts): the simulation (TOPA-PMX-TORI-2412) was fitted to toripalimab's own monotherapy studies including the 240 mg Q3W cohort, and CHOICE-01 had run on that regimen since 2019, so the model post-dates the drug's own patient result. It reproduced the observed exposure (Cmax/Cmin 85/19 vs 77/25 ug/mL): retro. The checker's proposed untested (post-hoc justification) is the alternative reading. No toripalimab opener on this track: the model's first use for toripalimab was first public in this same 2023 review.

efficacy.confidence_note: Study date 2015 is inferred from the study number ANA011.E004-RES-20150327 in the dostarlimab review; dostarlimab does not bind mouse PD-1, so the surrogate RMP1-14 was dosed.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in mice under PD-1 blockade (surrogate RMP1-14 in wild-type mice; toripalimab in human PD-1 knock-in mice)
efficacy.note: Surrogate anti-mouse PD-1 gave 78% tumour growth delay in MC38 and immunity to re-challenge; a class prediction, no member yet in NSCLC patients.
efficacy.short: Surrogate delays MC38; no patient test
efficacy.quote: Intraperitoneal injection of RMP1‐14 at 5 mg/kg twice weekly (Days 1, 4, 8, and 11) resulted in 78% tumor growth delay compared to Phosphate‐Buffer saline (PBS) vehicle control (n=6‐9/group)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 78% tumour growth delay in MC38 vs PFS hazard ratio 0.60
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of a Phase 3 with a PFS primary endpoint; NCT03134872 has no posted results. Year 2021, not the 2020-12-18 epub, because the member-specific model side (dostarlimab review) was public only from April 2021.
efficacy.judgement: Pairing with the class's MC38 surrogate model as filed by dostarlimab (product_in_model false). Camrelizumab's own human PD-1 transgenic MC38 data (20.4% inhibition, not significant; sponsor protocol for NCT03092895, public on ClinicalTrials.gov only from 2023-07-04) were not public in 2021, so the camrelizumab track opens with this pairing and has no earlier opener. CameL-sq (Ren 2022, 10.1016/j.jtho.2021.11.018) is the same direction.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in mice under PD-1 blockade (surrogate RMP1-14 in wild-type mice; toripalimab in human PD-1 knock-in mice)
efficacy.note: CameL (n=412): camrelizumab plus carboplatin-pemetrexed met PFS at interim (11.3 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.60). Combination ruling: scored on the trial's primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: Progression-free survival in this interim analysis was significantly prolonged with camrelizumab plus chemotherapy than with chemotherapy alone (median 11·3 months [95% CI 9·6-15·4] vs 8·3 months [6·0-9·7]; hazard ratio 0·60 [0·45-0·79]; one-sided p=0·0001).

patient_trials.quote: The primary endpoint was met at the interim analysis, showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival with camrelizumab plus carboplatin and pemetrexed versus chemotherapy alone in all patients

The results revealed significantly prolonged progression-free survival (median, 8.5 vs. 4.9 mo; p <0.0001) and overall survival (median, not reached vs. 14.5 mo; p <0.0001) with camrelizumab-chemotherapy versus placebo-chemotherapy.

efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track kept untested: the ex-vivo reactivation was compared with clinical response to nivolumab or pembrolizumab, neither a member; no member drug has been run on the platform.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived tumour fragments (NSCLC, melanoma) with ex-vivo PD-1 blockade
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo immune reactivation predicted clinical response, but only to non-member anti-PD-1 drugs; no member has been tested on the platform.
efficacy.short: Ex-vivo predictor tested with non-members only
efficacy.quote: We observed that the capacity of immune cells to be reactivated ex vivo was predictive of clinical response, and perturbation analyses identified tumor-resident T cells as a key component of this immunological response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: dose-dependent MC38 growth inhibition at >=1 mg/kg vs PFS hazard ratio 0.49
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of CHOICE-01 (JCO epub 2022-10-07, print 2023); year 2023 because toripalimab's own knock-in-mouse MC38 data became public in the October 2023 FDA review. Final OS (Wang 2024, 10.1038/s41392-024-02087-6): 23.8 vs 17.0 months, HR 0.69.
efficacy.judgement: Toripalimab's own track on the MC38 system (human PD-1 knock-in mice dosed with the product). Its model side and this pairing were both first public in the October 2023 FDA review, so no earlier toripalimab opener exists. Dostarlimab's PERLA and COSTAR Lung moved to the dostarlimab track (efficacy entry 7). Spartalizumab has no randomised NSCLC result.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in mice under PD-1 blockade (surrogate RMP1-14 in wild-type mice; toripalimab in human PD-1 knock-in mice)
efficacy.note: CHOICE-01 (n=465): toripalimab plus chemotherapy met PFS (HR 0.49) and interim OS (HR 0.69); the drug the knock-in mice were dosed with worked. Combination ruling: scored on the primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: At the final PFS analysis, PFS was significantly longer in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (median PFS, 8.4 v 5.6 months, hazard ratio = 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.61; two-sided P < .0001).

patient_trials.quote: At the interim OS analysis, the toripalimab arm had a significantly longer OS than the placebo arm (median OS not reached v 17.1 months, hazard ratio = 0.69; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.92; two-sided P = .0099).

efficacy.model: NSG mice bearing MC38 tumours engrafted with allogeneic human CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes, dosed with toripalimab (Study TR003)
efficacy.note: Immunodeficient NSG mice with MC38 and 2x10^7 allogeneic human CD8+ CTLs: CTLs alone did nothing, toripalimab 10 mg i.p. twice weekly gave minor antitumour activity.
efficacy.short: Allogeneic-CTL NSG mice: minor activity, untested
efficacy.quote: Engraftment of T cells alone had no antitumor activity and toripalimab (10 mg i.p. twice weekly) had minor antitumor activity in T cell-engrafted mice harboring allogeneic T cells (Figure 8).
efficacy.confidence_note: Review p.49 read in full; Figure 8 not quantified in the text, 'minor' is the FDA's word. The study is undated and predates toripalimab's March 2016 first-in-human dose; 2023 is its first public date.
efficacy.judgement: A separate track from mc38-mouse-pd1-blockade: the host is immunodeficient and the effector cells are transferred allogeneic human CTLs, not the mouse's own immunity, so the system and what it can predict differ from syngeneic or knock-in MC38.

efficacy.model: NSG mice bearing MC38 tumours engrafted with allogeneic human CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes, dosed with toripalimab (Study TR003)
efficacy.note: The product gave only minor activity in CTL-engrafted NSG mice; in CHOICE-01 toripalimab plus chemotherapy met PFS (HR 0.49) and interim OS in NSCLC.
efficacy.short: Minor mouse activity; CHOICE-01 PFS met
efficacy.quote: At the final PFS analysis, PFS was significantly longer in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (median PFS, 8.4 v 5.6 months, hazard ratio = 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.61; two-sided P < .0001).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of CHOICE-01 (JCO epub 2022-10-07, print 2023); NCT03856411 has no posted results. Year 2023 because the model side became public only in the October 2023 FDA review. Magnitude rests on the FDA's descriptor 'minor', not a number.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: 'minor antitumor activity' of toripalimab in CTL-engrafted NSG MC38 mice vs PFS hazard ratio 0.49 and interim OS hazard ratio 0.69 in CHOICE-01

patient_trials.quote: At the interim OS analysis, the toripalimab arm had a significantly longer OS than the placebo arm (median OS not reached v 17.1 months, hazard ratio = 0.69; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.92; two-sided P = .0099).

efficacy.judgement: Pairing is mine (comparison_stated false): the FDA review reports the model, CHOICE-01 the patients, and nobody set them side by side. Scored same because the model's direction was positive with a real window (CTLs alone inert), but partial: it under-called a drug that then gave HR 0.49. Whether an under-call of a drug that worked is same direction-only or should be set aside is the open rule question the checker raised for camrelizumab's model.
efficacy.reason: Minor mouse activity; drug worked in NSCLC

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MC38 78% growth delay with surrogate RMP1-14 vs PERLA ORR 45% (dostarlimab) vs 39% (pembrolizumab), each plus chemotherapy
efficacy.population: Metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, first line, no targetable alteration
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract and full-text passages read (Nat Commun epub 2023-11-11, PMID 37951954). Earliest public date: GSK press release and ESMO-IO 2022 abstract 57O, 2022-12-07 (ORR 46% vs 37% at the primary analysis).
efficacy.judgement: Split from entry 4: dostarlimab's track on the MC38 system it filed (surrogate RMP1-14, opener entry 1). Pairing is mine. COSTAR Lung (dostarlimab plus docetaxel after anti-PD-(L)1 progression, OS HR 0.96) is listed, not scored: acquired resistance after prior PD-1 blockade is a condition the naive-tumour mouse never modelled.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in mice under PD-1 blockade (surrogate RMP1-14 in wild-type mice; toripalimab in human PD-1 knock-in mice)
efficacy.note: PERLA (randomised phase II, dostarlimab vs pembrolizumab, each with chemotherapy): ORR 45% vs 39%, pre-specified endpoint met. Combination ruling: scored on its primary endpoint. First public at ESMO-IO, 2022-12-07.

patient_trials.quote: PERLA met its pre-specified endpoint. ORR (n/N; 95% CI) is 45% (55/121; 36.4-54.8) for DCT and 39% (48/122; 30.6-48.6) for PCT (data cut-off: 07 July 23), numerically favoring dostarlimab in PD-L1-positive subgroups.
Overall Survival (OS) (Arm B Versus Arm C): Dostarlimab + Docetaxel 11.8 months (10.3 to 12.9) vs Docetaxel 11.3 months (9.5 to 13.9); Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.96 (0.77 to 1.20)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; both FDA reviews cite PD-1-deficient mice in their nonclinical sections.
safety.note: Aged PD-1-null mice develop lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis: a standing prediction of autoimmunity from PD-1 loss before any patient was dosed.
safety.quote: Aged C57BL/6(B6)-PD-1(-/-) congenic mice spontaneously developed characteristic lupus-like proliferative arthritis and glomerulonephritis with predominant IgG3 deposition, which were markedly accelerated by introduction of a Fas mutation (lpr).

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the paper reports pharmacology and PK, not toxicology, so it carries no safety prediction.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
safety.note: First public monkey work with a member (JS-001 pharmacology and PK); no toxicity finding was reported to compare with patients.
safety.short: Monkey PK only, no safety call yet
safety.quote: These non-clinical data are encouraging and provide a basis for the efficacy and safety of JS-001 in clinical trials.

safety.magnitude_basis: off-target VEGFR2 agonism in vitro vs capillary haemangioma incidence in patients
safety.population: Advanced solid tumours in camrelizumab Phase 1 (not NSCLC-specific)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The system is an in-vitro human receptor-proteome screen on cultured cells; ex_vivo is the nearest enum. The patient side is the paper's own statement; the NSCLC rate of reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation sits in the CameL full text, not read. NSCLC patients show the same harm (NOAH-LC-101, 10.21037/tlcr-23-121: RCCEP in 18.6%, grade 1-2), so the retro status holds for this disease; year kept at the screen's own 2018 statement.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the screen was run because camrelizumab's capillary haemangiomas were already known from Phase 1 (Mo 2018), so retro, never same. A platform or molecule-specific harm, not an on-target one; no monkey toxicology for camrelizumab is public, so the species' silence is not scored.
safety.model: Human receptor-proteome screen of camrelizumab (SHR-1210) off-target binding
safety.note: Run after the harm was known: camrelizumab bound and agonised VEGFR2 off-target, explaining its unique capillary haemangiomas; paratope refinement removed the binding.
safety.quote: As the humanized antibody SHR-1210 causes capillary hemangioma in patients, a unique toxicity amongst anti-PD1 antibodies, we performed human receptor proteome screening to identify nonspecific interactions that might drive angiogenesis.

safety.magnitude_basis: organ pattern: arthritis and glomerulonephritis in mice vs thyroid, skin, lung and liver immune-mediated reactions in patients
safety.population: Treatment-naive advanced NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations (CHOICE-01)
safety.confidence_note: Full-text passage of CHOICE-01 read (PMC9870236); CameL full text, which may report irAEs earlier (2020), not read.
safety.judgement: Pairing is mine: Nishimura's lupus-like autoimmunity against immune-related adverse events in NSCLC patients on a member drug. Directional only: patients' organs (thyroid, skin, lung) differ from the mouse's joints and kidney. Previously scored on dostarlimab's endometrial patients (2021); under the imported-harm ruling the NSCLC result replaces them.
safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: NSCLC patients were measured, so they decide. CHOICE-01: immune-related events in 49.4% on toripalimab vs 21.2% on placebo, the autoimmunity the knockout foretold.
safety.quote: irAEs, as assessed by blinded investigators, were more frequent in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (49.4% v 21.2%; Data Supplement).

safety.confidence_note: Review read in passages. FDA hedged: the skin lesion and the kidney, liver and heart infiltrates were sporadic, not dose-related, and 'could be' pharmacological; the clinical statement follows in the same paragraph.
safety.judgement: Opener of the dostarlimab track on the monkey system. It was scored same on dostarlimab's endometrial patients; since NSCLC patients on dostarlimab were later measured (PERLA), the imported result is set aside and the NSCLC comparison is entry 7.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
safety.note: Dostarlimab monkeys: minimal infiltrates and one immune-type skin lesion. Imported-harm ruling: the endometrial result no longer scores, and no NSCLC patient safety data existed in 2021.
safety.short: Monkey immune lesions; no NSCLC data yet
safety.quote: The majority of microscopic findings in surviving animals was minimal mononuclear cell infiltration in numerous tissues, consistent with the mechanism of action.

safety.magnitude_basis: no toxicity in monkeys at 13-23x patient exposure vs immune-related events in 25-40% of patients with fatal pneumonitis
safety.population: Treatment-naive advanced NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations (CHOICE-01)
safety.confidence_note: Monkey sentence from the 761240 review (p.43; FDA: no toripalimab-related adverse effects up to 100 mg/kg); patient side from CHOICE-01 full text (PMC9870236). Year stays 2023, the model side's first public date.
safety.judgement: Contra on toripalimab's own monkey track: the monkeys, dosed weekly for 26 weeks with the receptor saturated, showed nothing, while NSCLC patients had immune-related events in 49.4% vs 21.2% on placebo. The dostarlimab monkeys show the species can display the lesion, so the silence counts. Dostarlimab's monkeys are a separate track (entries 5 and 7). Patient side moved from NPC and pooled tumours to NSCLC under the imported-harm ruling.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
safety.note: Toripalimab monkeys at 13-23x patient exposure for 26 weeks showed no toxicity; in CHOICE-01 NSCLC patients had immune-related events in 49.4% (15.6% grade 3 or worse). Imported-harm ruling: NSCLC decides.
safety.quote: irAEs, as assessed by blinded investigators, were more frequent in the toripalimab arm than in the placebo arm (49.4% v 21.2%; Data Supplement).
safety.reason: Knockout right, monkeys split, haemangioma retrodicted

safety.magnitude_basis: minimal infiltrates and one immune-type skin lesion in monkeys vs immune-related events in 31% of NSCLC patients
safety.confidence_note: PERLA full text read in passages (PMC10640551, epub 2023-11-11); registry results 2023-09-18. The ESMO-IO 2022 abstract (2022-12-07) may carry safety earlier; not read.
safety.judgement: Pairing is mine. Same in direction, partial in size (one monkey with immune-type skin inflammation, sporadic infiltrates; FDA hedged them as possibly pharmacological). Imported-harm ruling: the NSCLC result replaces the endometrial one (entry 5).
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey pharmacology and repeat-dose toxicology with a PD-1 receptor-occupancy readout (toripalimab, dostarlimab)
safety.note: PERLA: immune-related events in 31% of NSCLC patients on dostarlimab plus chemotherapy, the immune-type harm the monkeys showed in mild form. Partial: minimal in monkeys, frequent in patients.
safety.short: NSCLC irAEs 31%, monkeys showed mild form
safety.quote: a numerical trend favoring dostarlimab was observed in the proportion of patients experiencing immune-related adverse events (irAEs) (31% for dostarlimab plus chemotherapy and 39% for pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy)
safety.reason: Monkey immune lesions matched in NSCLC
